name: Geography
description: A survey of physical and human geography — Earth's landforms, climate zones, ecosystems, world regions, cultural patterns, economic systems, and the relationship between people and place.

modules.title: Introduction to Geography
modules.objectives: Identify the five themes of geography; explain how maps, GPS, and geographic tools help us understand the world; locate places using latitude and longitude.
modules.readingNote: National Geographic Education — Geography Standard 1 — maps, geospatial technologies, and spatial thinking
modules.videoNote: GIIS — Module 1: Introduction to Geography lesson video
modules.practiceNote: GIIS Learn Portal — use the module lesson, assigned course materials, and teacher-reviewed practice inside the GIIS course path; no external practice platform is required.
modules.assignment: Choose any location on Earth. Use latitude and longitude to identify it, then describe it using all five themes of geography (location, place, human-environment interaction, movement, region). Submit: one map, table, annotated visual, or short report. Include: the requested locations or data, at least two cited sources, and a paragraph explaining the geographic pattern or relationship. Evaluation: accurate evidence, readable labels, sound comparison, and a direct connection to the module objectives.

modules.title: Physical Geography: Landforms
modules.objectives: Identify the seven continents and major landforms; explain how tectonic plates shape Earth's surface; describe the formation of mountains, rivers, and plains.
modules.videoNote: GIIS — Module 2: Physical Geography: Landforms lesson video
modules.practiceNote: National Geographic Education — Plate Boundaries — how convergent, divergent, and transform boundaries shape landforms and hazards
modules.assignment: Create a labeled diagram of Earth's major landform types (mountains, plains, plateaus, valleys, rivers). For each, name one real-world example and the continent where it is found. Submit: one map, table, annotated visual, or short report. Include: the requested locations or data, at least two cited sources, and a paragraph explaining the geographic pattern or relationship. Evaluation: accurate evidence, readable labels, sound comparison, and a direct connection to the module objectives.

modules.title: Climate & Weather Patterns
modules.objectives: Distinguish between weather and climate; identify the major climate zones using the Köppen classification system; explain factors that influence climate.
modules.readingNote: NOAA — What’s the Difference Between Climate and Weather? — timescale, evidence, and common measures
modules.videoNote: GIIS — Module 3: Climate & Weather Patterns lesson video
modules.practiceNote: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory — Worldwide Climate Zones — mapped climate-zone practice and interpretation
modules.assignment: Compare two cities with different climate types (e.g., Singapore vs. Cairo). For each city, identify the Köppen classification, describe typical seasonal conditions, and explain what geographic factors cause those conditions. Submit: one map, table, annotated visual, or short report. Include: the requested locations or data, at least two cited sources, and a paragraph explaining the geographic pattern or relationship. Evaluation: accurate evidence, readable labels, sound comparison, and a direct connection to the module objectives.

modules.title: World Ecosystems
modules.objectives: Identify major world biomes including rainforests, deserts, grasslands, and tundra; explain how climate determines ecosystem type; describe key plant and animal adaptations.
modules.videoNote: GIIS — Module 4: World Ecosystems lesson video
modules.practiceNote: National Geographic Education — Geography Standard 8 — ecosystem distributions, characteristics, and processes across Earth
modules.assignment: Select two contrasting biomes (e.g., tropical rainforest and tundra). Create a comparison table covering climate, plant life, animal life, and human impact. Then write a paragraph explaining how each biome's climate shapes its living community. Submit: one map, table, annotated visual, or short report. Include: the requested locations or data, at least two cited sources, and a paragraph explaining the geographic pattern or relationship. Evaluation: accurate evidence, readable labels, sound comparison, and a direct connection to the module objectives.

modules.title: Human Geography: Population
modules.objectives: Explain global population distribution and density patterns; analyze demographic trends including birth rate, death rate, and natural increase; understand urbanization.
modules.readingNote: National Geographic Education — Population Density — distribution, density, and geographic constraints
modules.videoNote: GIIS — Module 5: Human Geography: Population lesson video
modules.practiceNote: World Bank Open Data — Country profiles and World Development Indicators for comparable population measures
modules.assignment: Using World Bank Open Data, compare one high-income country and one low-income country using the latest common year available for population density, crude birth rate, and urban population percentage. Record the indicator name, value, unit, year, and source for each figure. Explain two geographic or social patterns the data may suggest and one limitation that prevents the three indicators from proving a single 'stage of development.' Submit: one cited comparison table plus a short analysis. Include: the requested data, at least two source links, and a paragraph explaining the geographic pattern or relationship. Evaluation: accurate evidence, comparable years and units, cautious interpretation, readable labels, and a direct connection to the module objectives.

modules.title: Culture & Identity
modules.objectives: Define culture and its components; explain how language, religion, and ethnicity shape cultural regions; analyze cultural diffusion and the effects of globalization.
modules.readingNote: National Geographic Education — Global Network — how cultural ideas, products, and practices move and change through global connections
modules.videoNote: GIIS — Module 6: Culture & Identity lesson video
modules.practiceNote: National Geographic Education — Geography Standard 10 — cultural mosaics, diffusion, and changing cultural patterns
modules.assignment: Identify one example of cultural diffusion you see in your own daily life (food, music, language, clothing, etc.). Trace where the cultural element originated, how it spread, and how — if at all — it changed as it moved into new regions. Submit: one map, table, annotated visual, or short report. Include: the requested locations or data, at least two cited sources, and a paragraph explaining the geographic pattern or relationship. Evaluation: accurate evidence, readable labels, sound comparison, and a direct connection to the module objectives.

modules.title: Political Geography
modules.objectives: Distinguish between different types of political boundaries; explain the concept of sovereignty and the nation-state; compare types of government around the world.
modules.readingNote: National Geographic Education — Geography Standard 13 — sovereignty, boundaries, territorial divisions, cooperation, and conflict
modules.videoNote: GIIS — Module 7: Political Geography lesson video
modules.practiceNote: Constitute Project — searchable primary constitutional texts for comparing formal government structures and rights
modules.assignment: Choose two countries with different constitutional structures. Use the Constitute Project and one additional reliable source for each country to compare the executive-legislative relationship, territorial organization (unitary or federal), and one formally protected right or civic responsibility. Distinguish what the constitutional text establishes from what would require evidence about implementation or daily life. Submit: one cited comparison table plus a short analysis. Include: the requested evidence, at least two source links, and a paragraph explaining how sovereignty or territorial organization shapes the comparison. Evaluation: accurate evidence, careful distinction between formal rules and lived outcomes, readable labels, and a direct connection to the module objectives.

modules.title: Economic Geography
modules.objectives: Compare economies using GDP per capita, sector structure, and HDI while explaining the limits of any single measure; explain patterns of global trade and the role of supply chains; analyze how geography influences economic activity.
modules.readingNote: National Geographic Education — Geography Standard 11 — economic activity, trade networks, and spatial interdependence
modules.videoNote: GIIS — Module 8: Economic Geography lesson video
modules.practiceNote: United Nations Development Programme — Country Insights — current HDI profiles and multidimensional development indicators
modules.assignment: Compare one high-income country and one low-income country using the latest comparable World Bank GDP-per-capita and sector data plus UNDP Human Development Index data. Record each indicator's value, unit, and year. Identify one geographic advantage and one geographic constraint for economic activity in each country, then explain why GDP per capita alone does not establish a complete development ranking. Submit: one cited comparison table plus a short analysis. Include: the requested data, at least two source links, and a paragraph explaining the geographic pattern or relationship. Evaluation: accurate evidence, comparable years and units, multidimensional reasoning, readable labels, and a direct connection to the module objectives.

questions.question: Which of the five themes of geography asks 'How do humans change the environment and how does the environment change humans?'
questions.answer: Human-Environment Interaction
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Human-Environment Interaction. Students need to recognize why Human-Environment Interaction matches the evidence in the question and why nearby options do not.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the direction and measurement of latitude lines?
options: North–south, measuring distance from the prime meridian
East–west, measuring distance from the equator
questions.answer: East–west, measuring distance from the equator
questions.explanation: Latitude lines run east–west and measure angular distance north or south of the equator; longitude lines run north–south.

questions.question: Tectonic plates move because of:
questions.answer: Convection currents in Earth's mantle
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Convection currents in Earth's mantle. It ties the answer to the historical, civic, geographic, or economic concept being assessed.

questions.question: Which option best completes this statement? The Himalayas were formed by:
options: A convergent boundary between the Indian and Eurasian plates
A divergent boundary in the Atlantic Ocean
A hotspot under the Pacific Plate
Wind erosion across a desert basin
questions.answer: A convergent boundary between the Indian and Eurasian plates
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: A convergent boundary between the Indian and Eurasian plates.

questions.question: The Köppen climate classification system categorizes climates primarily based on:
questions.answer: Temperature and precipitation patterns
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Temperature and precipitation patterns. Students need to recognize why Temperature and precipitation patterns matches the evidence in the question and why nearby options do not.

questions.question: Which Köppen climate group is defined by dryness because precipitation is insufficient relative to potential evapotranspiration?
questions.answer: Dry/arid (B)
questions.explanation: Köppen B climates are classified by an aridity threshold that compares precipitation with estimated moisture demand, distinguishing dry climates from polar E climates even when both may receive little precipitation.

questions.question: The tropical rainforest biome is characterized by:
options: High biodiversity, year-round warmth, and heavy rainfall
questions.answer: High biodiversity, year-round warmth, and heavy rainfall
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: High biodiversity, year-round warmth, and heavy rainfall.

questions.question: Which option best completes this statement? The tundra biome is found primarily:
options: In high-latitude Arctic regions and some high mountains
questions.answer: In high-latitude Arctic regions and some high mountains
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: In high-latitude Arctic regions and some high mountains.

questions.question: Population density is calculated as:
options: Total population divided by total area
Total area divided by total population
Urban population divided by rural population
questions.answer: Total population divided by total area
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Total population divided by total area. The explanation asks students to connect the answer with cause, evidence, or consequence rather than memorizing a term.

questions.question: Which population change is described by the term urbanization?
options: The shift of people from rural areas to cities
questions.answer: The shift of people from rural areas to cities
questions.explanation: Urbanization is the increase in the share of people living in urban areas, often driven by rural-to-urban migration and natural growth in cities.

questions.question: Cultural diffusion is best described as:
options: The isolation of one culture from outside influences
The spread of cultural elements from one group to another
The extinction of a minority language
questions.answer: The spread of cultural elements from one group to another
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: The spread of cultural elements from one group to another.

questions.question: Which example best demonstrates cultural diffusion?
options: A musical style spreads to another region and blends with local traditions
A mountain range forms at a convergent plate boundary
A river erodes a canyon over time
A country calculates its population density
questions.answer: A musical style spreads to another region and blends with local traditions
questions.explanation: Cultural diffusion is the spread of cultural traits between places or groups; those traits may be adopted, adapted, or combined with local practices.

questions.question: Sovereignty means a state has:
options: Supreme authority over its own territory and affairs
questions.answer: Supreme authority over its own territory and affairs
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Supreme authority over its own territory and affairs.

questions.question: Explain the difference between a 'nation' and a 'state' in political geography, and give one real-world example of a nation without a state.
questions.answer: A 'state' is a politically organized territory with sovereignty; a 'nation' is a group of people sharing common culture, language, or history. An example of a nation without a state is the Kurds, a people with a distinct culture spread across Turkey, Iraq, Iran, and Syria without their own sovereign country.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: A 'state' is a politically organized territory with sovereignty; a 'nation' is a group of people sharing common culture, language, or history. An example of a nation without a state is the Kurds, a people with a distinct culture spread across Turkey, Iraq, Iran, and Syria without their own sovereign country..

questions.question: GDP per capita is most useful for comparing:
options: Average economic output per person across countries
The size of a country's military
questions.answer: Average economic output per person across countries
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Average economic output per person across countries.

questions.question: In this course, which of the following is an example of an absolute location?
questions.answer: A latitude and longitude coordinate
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: A latitude and longitude coordinate. Students need to recognize why A latitude and longitude coordinate matches the evidence in the question and why nearby options do not.

questions.question: Which major landform is created when two tectonic plates diverge on land?
questions.answer: Rift valley
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Rift valley. The choice fits the prompt because it applies the central rule or concept from Geography final concepts.

questions.question: A region near the equator with high temperatures year-round and two distinct wet/dry seasons is classified as:
questions.answer: Tropical savanna
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Tropical savanna. The choice fits the prompt because it applies the central rule or concept from Geography final concepts.

questions.question: Which statement best explains why tropical rainforests support high biodiversity?
options: Year-round warmth and moisture support high productivity and many ecological niches
Permanent permafrost supplies abundant liquid water
A short growing season favors only a few species
questions.answer: Year-round warmth and moisture support high productivity and many ecological niches
questions.explanation: Consistent warmth, abundant moisture, layered vegetation, and high productivity create many habitats and resources, supporting diverse species.

questions.question: Which option best completes this statement? The demographic transition model predicts that as countries develop economically:
options: Death rates usually fall first, then birth rates decline later
Birth and death rates rise forever
Birth rates fall before any change in death rates
Population change becomes unrelated to health or income
questions.answer: Death rates usually fall first, then birth rates decline later
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Death rates usually fall first, then birth rates decline later.

questions.question: Globalization has most directly accelerated cultural diffusion by:
options: Expanding internet access and mass media worldwide
questions.answer: Expanding internet access and mass media worldwide
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Expanding internet access and mass media worldwide. The choice fits the prompt because it applies the central rule or concept from Geography final concepts.

questions.question: A unitary government system is one in which:
options: Power is shared equally between states and the federal government
Central government holds most political power
Multiple political parties share executive power
questions.answer: Central government holds most political power
questions.explanation: In a unitary system, the central government is sovereign and may delegate powers to local governments rather than sharing constitutionally protected authority with states.

questions.question: A global supply chain means that a product's components are:
options: Produced in multiple countries and assembled elsewhere
Traded only within a single trade bloc
questions.answer: Produced in multiple countries and assembled elsewhere
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Produced in multiple countries and assembled elsewhere.

questions.question: A map uses darker colors to show higher annual precipitation by county. What type of information does the map communicate most directly?
options: The spatial pattern of precipitation values
The cause of every rainfall event
The exact weather at this moment
The political system of each county
questions.answer: The spatial pattern of precipitation values
questions.explanation: A thematic map can show how a measured variable varies across space. By itself, it does not prove causes or give current weather conditions.

questions.question: The Amazon River basin, the world's largest by discharge, is located in:
questions.answer: South America
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: South America. The choice fits the prompt because it applies the central rule or concept from Geography final concepts.

questions.question: Some resource-dependent countries experience weak diversification, price volatility, governance pressures, and poverty despite large mineral or petroleum revenues. What conditional pattern is this sometimes called?
questions.answer: The resource curse
questions.explanation: The resource curse describes a possible pattern in some resource-dependent economies; resource abundance alone does not cause or prove the outcome. Institutions, diversification, revenue management, conflict, and global markets shape results.

questions.question: Water scarcity in the Middle East and North Africa is primarily caused by:
options: Arid climate, high evaporation, and rapidly growing populations
questions.answer: Arid climate, high evaporation, and rapidly growing populations
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: Arid climate, high evaporation, and rapidly growing populations.

questions.question: Which option best completes this statement? The monsoon is a seasonal wind pattern that brings heavy rainfall primarily to:
questions.answer: South and Southeast Asia
questions.explanation: Seasonal monsoon wind shifts strongly affect South and Southeast Asia, bringing much of the region’s annual rainfall during the summer monsoon.

questions.question: Country A has 48 million people and 600,000 km² of land area. What is its population density?
questions.answer: 80 people per km²
questions.explanation: Population density equals population divided by land area: 48,000,000 ÷ 600,000 = 80 people per km².

questions.question: Pacific Island nations like Tuvalu and Kiribati face an existential threat from:
options: Rising sea levels due to climate change
questions.answer: Rising sea levels due to climate change
questions.explanation: Low-lying atolls in Tuvalu and Kiribati are highly exposed to sea-level rise, erosion, saltwater intrusion, and storm surge.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a federal state from a unitary state?
options: A federal constitution divides authority between national and regional governments; a unitary system places ultimate authority at the national level
A federal state has no national government; a unitary state has no local governments
Federalism guarantees democracy; a unitary system prevents it
Only unitary states have written constitutions
questions.answer: A federal constitution divides authority between national and regional governments; a unitary system places ultimate authority at the national level
questions.explanation: Federal systems constitutionally divide authority across levels. Unitary states may delegate powers locally, but the national government retains ultimate legal authority; neither structure alone determines democratic practice.

questions.question: A food tradition moves through migration, adopts local ingredients, and becomes part of a new region’s cuisine. Which process does this illustrate?
questions.answer: Cultural diffusion and adaptation
questions.explanation: The tradition spreads between regions and changes through contact with local practices, illustrating both diffusion and adaptation.

questions.question: Why should GDP per capita and HDI be considered together when comparing countries?
options: GDP per capita measures average economic output, while HDI also includes health and education dimensions
HDI measures only exports, while GDP measures climate
Either measure proves how every individual lives
questions.answer: GDP per capita measures average economic output, while HDI also includes health and education dimensions
questions.explanation: GDP per capita summarizes average economic output but not its distribution or non-income outcomes. HDI adds health and education indicators, so the measures provide different evidence and still do not describe every person’s experience.

questions.question: Choose two locations you analyzed in your completed module assignments. Using the sources you cited there, compare how one physical-geography factor and one human-geography factor shape a measurable pattern in each location. State one limitation of your comparison.
questions.answer: Answers will vary. A complete response identifies two previously studied locations, cites the student’s assignment evidence, and compares a physical factor such as climate, landform, or water access plus a human factor such as migration, policy, trade, or infrastructure. It must connect each factor to a measurable pattern without claiming that geography determines outcomes and must state one limitation involving source quality, scale, date, comparability, or causation.
questions.explanation: Score for two identified locations, two cited sources from completed work, one physical and one human factor, evidence-linked comparison, and a valid limitation. Do not award full credit for unsupported regional stereotypes or deterministic claims.

questions.question: Which organization is primarily responsible for promoting free trade among its member nations through tariff reductions and trade agreements?
questions.answer: World Trade Organization (WTO)
questions.explanation: The correct answer is: World Trade Organization (WTO). Students need to recognize why World Trade Organization (WTO) matches the evidence in the question and why nearby options do not.

quizQuestions.question: Which of the five themes of geography refers to a specific spot on Earth identified by coordinates?
quizQuestions.explanation: The correct answer is: Location. Students need to recognize why Location matches the evidence in the question and why nearby options do not.

quizQuestions.question: Lines of latitude are also called:
quizQuestions.explanation: Lines of latitude are parallel to the equator, so they are called parallels; meridians are lines of longitude.

quizQuestions.question: Which geographic technology stores and analyzes layers of spatial data?
quizQuestions.explanation: A geographic information system (GIS) combines layers such as roads, elevation, and population so users can analyze spatial relationships.

quizQuestions.question: How many continents does Earth have?
quizQuestions.explanation: The seven-continent model used in this course names Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, and Australia.

quizQuestions.question: Which landform is an elevated flat-topped area?
quizQuestions.explanation: The correct answer is: Plateau. Students need to recognize why Plateau matches the evidence in the question and why nearby options do not.

quizQuestions.question: Tectonic plates that move apart from each other form:
quizQuestions.explanation: At a divergent boundary, two plates move away from one another and new crust can form between them.

quizQuestions.question: Which feature commonly forms where continental crust pulls apart at a divergent boundary?
quizQuestions.explanation: As continental crust stretches and thins, blocks can drop along faults and form a rift valley, such as the East African Rift.

quizQuestions.question: In Climate & Weather Patterns, Weather refers to:
options: Long-term atmospheric patterns in an area
Short-term atmospheric conditions at a specific time and place
quizQuestions.answer: Short-term atmospheric conditions at a specific time and place
quizQuestions.explanation: The correct answer is: Short-term atmospheric conditions at a specific time and place.

quizQuestions.question: Tropical climate zones are located:
quizQuestions.explanation: The tropics lie around the equator, where sunlight is relatively direct throughout the year.

quizQuestions.question: The main driver of global wind and ocean current patterns is:
options: Unequal heating of Earth's surface by the sun
quizQuestions.answer: Unequal heating of Earth's surface by the sun
quizQuestions.explanation: Uneven solar heating creates pressure and density differences that drive atmospheric circulation and help drive ocean currents.

quizQuestions.question: In World Ecosystems, A biome is best defined as:
options: A large naturally occurring community of plants and animals adapted to a specific climate
quizQuestions.answer: A large naturally occurring community of plants and animals adapted to a specific climate
quizQuestions.explanation: The correct answer is: A large naturally occurring community of plants and animals adapted to a specific climate.

quizQuestions.question: The Amazon rainforest is located primarily in:
quizQuestions.explanation: Most of the Amazon rainforest lies within Brazil in South America, although it extends into several neighboring countries.

quizQuestions.question: Which biome receives the least precipitation?
quizQuestions.explanation: The correct answer is: Desert. It ties the answer to the historical, civic, geographic, or economic concept being assessed.

quizQuestions.question: Permafrost is a feature of which biome?
quizQuestions.explanation: The correct answer is: Tundra. Students need to recognize why Tundra matches the evidence in the question and why nearby options do not.

quizQuestions.question: Using density = population ÷ area, which region is most densely populated?
options: Region A: 200 million people over 2 million km²
Region B: 300 million people over 6 million km²
Region C: 80 million people over 2 million km²
Region D: 50 million people over 5 million km²
quizQuestions.answer: Region A: 200 million people over 2 million km²
quizQuestions.explanation: Region A has 100 people per km²; Regions B, C, and D have 50, 40, and 10 people per km². Density requires dividing population by consistently defined area.

quizQuestions.question: The natural rate of population increase equals:
options: Total fertility rate divided by population
quizQuestions.explanation: The correct answer is: Birth rate minus death rate. The choice fits the prompt because it applies the central rule or concept from Human Geography: Population.

quizQuestions.question: A region has 2,000,000 people living in 50,000 square kilometers. What is its population density?
quizQuestions.explanation: Population density equals population divided by area: 2,000,000 ÷ 50,000 = 40 people per square kilometer.

quizQuestions.question: Which measure compares the nonworking-age population with the working-age population?
quizQuestions.explanation: The dependency ratio compares children and older adults with the working-age population that may support them economically.

quizQuestions.question: Which is the most widely spoken language family in the world?
quizQuestions.explanation: The correct answer is: Indo-European. It ties the answer to the historical, civic, geographic, or economic concept being assessed.

quizQuestions.question: In Culture & Identity, A lingua franca is:
options: A language spoken only in France
A common language used between speakers of different native languages
quizQuestions.answer: A common language used between speakers of different native languages
quizQuestions.explanation: The correct answer is: A common language used between speakers of different native languages.

quizQuestions.question: The spread of McDonald's restaurants around the world is an example of:
quizQuestions.explanation: The correct answer is: Cultural diffusion through globalization. It ties the answer to the historical, civic, geographic, or economic concept being assessed.

quizQuestions.question: Which example best shows cultural diffusion?
options: A food tradition spreads to another region and adapts to local ingredients
A mountain range forms at a plate boundary
A city records a lower birth rate
A river changes course after a flood
quizQuestions.answer: A food tradition spreads to another region and adapts to local ingredients
quizQuestions.explanation: Cultural diffusion occurs when an idea or practice moves between groups; local adaptation can change it during that movement.

quizQuestions.question: In Political Geography, A nation-state is:
options: Any large country with a big military
A political unit in which the state's borders match the cultural nation
A country ruled by a king
quizQuestions.answer: A political unit in which the state's borders match the cultural nation
quizQuestions.explanation: The correct answer is: A political unit in which the state's borders match the cultural nation.

quizQuestions.question: A federal system of government divides power between:
quizQuestions.explanation: The correct answer is: National and regional/state governments. The choice fits the prompt because it applies the central rule or concept from Political Geography.

quizQuestions.question: Which feature distinguishes a federal system from a unitary system?
options: Constitutionally divided power between national and regional governments
quizQuestions.answer: Constitutionally divided power between national and regional governments
quizQuestions.explanation: Federal constitutions assign authority to both national and regional governments; unitary systems concentrate sovereignty at the center.

quizQuestions.question: In Economic Geography, GDP stands for:
quizQuestions.explanation: GDP means gross domestic product, the market value of final goods and services produced within a country over a period.

quizQuestions.question: Which sector of the economy involves extracting natural resources?
quizQuestions.explanation: The correct answer is: Primary sector. Students need to recognize why Primary sector matches the evidence in the question and why nearby options do not.

quizQuestions.question: Comparative advantage exists when a producer can make a good at:
options: A lower opportunity cost than another producer
A higher money price than every competitor
The greatest absolute output in all goods
quizQuestions.answer: A lower opportunity cost than another producer
quizQuestions.explanation: Comparative advantage is based on lower opportunity cost, not simply higher productivity or absolute output. It explains potential gains from specialization and trade.

quizQuestions.question: Which activity belongs to the secondary sector of an economy?
quizQuestions.explanation: The secondary sector transforms raw materials into manufactured goods; mining is primary, while services and knowledge work are tertiary or quaternary.
